title: CT4109 Digital Image Processing & Computer Vision — Practice Examination Questions: Weeks 1–4

questions.title: Exam information and instructions
questions.prompt:
University of Galway
CT4109 Digital Image Processing & Computer Vision
Practice Examination Questions: Camera Calibration, Epipolar Geometry and Stereo Matching
Weeks 1–4
Time allowed: 3 hours. Total: 180 marks.

Attempt all questions. Marks for each part are shown in brackets. Show all working. Non-programmable calculators are permitted. Homogeneous points are column vectors; x ≃ y means equal up to a non-zero scale.

questions.title: Q1 — Homogeneous coordinates
questions.prompt:
(a) Write the inhomogeneous point (3, 4) in two different homogeneous forms, and convert (6, 9, 3)^T back. [2 marks]
(b) Find the line l through (1, 1) and (3, 5) using a cross product. [2 marks]
(c) Find the intersection of l with the line x = 0, i.e. (1, 0, 0)^T. [2 marks]

questions.title: Q2 — Transformation hierarchy
questions.prompt:
(a) State the degrees of freedom of a 2D Euclidean, similarity, affine and projective transformation. [4 marks]
(b) For each, state which of {parallelism, ratio of lengths on a line, angles, cross-ratio} is preserved. [2 marks]
(c) How many point correspondences are needed to estimate a 2D homography, and why? [2 marks]

questions.title: Q3 — Rotation matrices
questions.prompt:
Let R be the rotation of 90 degrees about the z-axis.
(a) Write R and verify R^T R = I, det R = 1. [3 marks]
(b) Compute R^(-1) without a general inverse and rotate (1, 2, 3)^T. [2 marks]
(c) A rotation Rx(90 degrees) is applied after R. Write the combined matrix and say whether the order matters. [3 marks]

questions.title: Q4 — Pinhole projection and units
questions.prompt:
A camera has f = 8 mm, square pixels of 5 micrometres and a 1280 x 960 sensor, principal point at the centre.
(a) Compute fx = fy in pixels and write K. [3 marks]
(b) Project the camera-frame point (0.5, -0.2, 5) m. [3 marks]
(c) The same point moves to Z = 10 m. What happens to its offset from the principal point? [2 marks]

questions.title: Q5 — Camera pose and projection matrix
questions.prompt:
K = [[800, 0, 320], [0, 800, 240], [0, 0, 1]], R = I, camera centre C = (0, 0, -2)^T.
(a) Find t and the matrix P = K[R | t]. [3 marks]
(b) Project the world point (0.25, 0.125, 3)^T. [3 marks]
(c) Explain why P has 11 degrees of freedom. [2 marks]

questions.title: Q6 — Inverse mapping: road-width measurement
questions.prompt:
A forward-looking camera views the road plane. The ground-to-image homography (ground in cm) is H = [[2, 0, 100], [0, 1, 50], [0, 0.002, 1]]. The left and right kerb edges appear at pixels (200, 200) and (600, 200).
(a) Compute H^(-1) (up to scale is acceptable). [4 marks]
(b) Map both kerb pixels to ground coordinates. [3 marks]
(c) State the road width in metres. Why would simply subtracting the pixel coordinates (400 px) be wrong? [3 marks]

questions.title: Q7 — Inverse mapping: surgical instrument
questions.prompt:
A calibrated overhead camera views the operating field (a plane). The field-to-image homography (mm) is H = [[1, 0, 0], [0, 1, 0], [0.002, 0.001, 1]]. The tip and tail of an instrument appear at pixels (250, 0) and (125, 250).
(a) Write H^(-1). [3 marks]
(b) Compute the tip and tail positions in mm. [4 marks]
(c) Compute the instrument length. Give two reasons the result may be wrong by several mm in practice and one way the 4-point calibration could be improved. [3 marks]

questions.title: Q8 — Pure rotation homography
questions.prompt:
Camera K = [[800, 0, 320], [0, 800, 240], [0, 0, 1]] pans by 10 degrees about its y-axis (no translation).
(a) Give the formula for the homography H between the two images. [2 marks]
(b) Where does the principal point (320, 240) of image 1 appear in image 2 (use Ry(10 degrees))? [4 marks]
(c) Why can no depth be recovered from two images related by a pure rotation? [2 marks]

questions.title: Q9 — Direct Linear Transform
questions.prompt:
(a) How many equations does each 3D-2D correspondence give for P, and what is the minimum number of points? [3 marks]
(b) Describe how the solution is obtained from A p = 0 (SVD) and why normalisation of points helps. [3 marks]
(c) Name one degenerate configuration of the 3D points and explain the effect. [2 marks]
(d) How are K, R and t recovered from P = [M | p4]? [2 marks]

questions.title: Q10 — Essential matrix and epipolar lines
questions.prompt:
Two normalised cameras: R = I, t = (0, 0, 1)^T (the second camera moves forward along the optical axis).
(a) Write E = [t]_x R. [3 marks]
(b) For x = (0.2, 0.1, 1)^T in image 1, compute the epipolar line l' = E x in image 2. [3 marks]
(c) Where are the epipoles? What is distinctive about the epipolar lines for forward motion? [4 marks]

questions.title: Q11 — Fundamental matrix
questions.prompt:
(a) State the epipolar constraint and the relation between F and E. [3 marks]
(b) Give the degrees of freedom of E and F and explain why det F = 0. [3 marks]
(c) How many correspondences does the (linear) 8-point algorithm need and what step enforces rank 2? [2 marks]

questions.title: Q12 — Rectification and triangulation
questions.prompt:
(a) What does rectification do to the epipolar lines and the epipoles? [3 marks]
(b) Why does rectification reduce stereo matching to a 1D search? [2 marks]
(c) Four (R, t) decompositions of E exist. How is the correct one chosen (chirality)? [3 marks]

questions.title: Q13 — Disparity and depth
questions.prompt:
A rectified rig has f = 1000 px and baseline B = 0.2 m.
(a) Compute the depth for disparities 40, 25 and 10 px. [3 marks]
(b) The depth precision at Z = 20 m for a +/-1 px disparity error. [3 marks]
(c) Doubling the baseline: effect on range, precision and on matching difficulty? [2 marks]

questions.title: Q14 — Block matching by hand
questions.prompt:
A 3 x 3 left window is L = [[10, 20, 30], [40, 50, 60], [70, 80, 90]]. Two candidate right windows are R0 = [[12, 22, 28], [38, 52, 61], [72, 79, 93]] and R1 = [[50, 60, 70], [80, 90, 100], [10, 20, 30]].
(a) Compute SAD and SSD for both candidates. [4 marks]
(b) Which disparity is chosen by winner-takes-all? [2 marks]
(c) Why are SSD costs more sensitive to outliers? [2 marks]
(d) Name two image conditions where this window matching fails. [2 marks]

questions.title: Q15 — Local versus global methods
questions.prompt:
(a) Explain the effect of window size on accuracy at depth edges and in low-texture regions. [3 marks]
(b) What does the smoothness term (penalties P1, P2) add in scanline/semi-global methods? [3 marks]
(c) Describe the left-right consistency check and which pixels it rejects. [2 marks]
(d) A viewer sees a depth map with a flat wall labelled at the wrong depth in a repeating tile pattern. Diagnose and suggest two remedies. [2 marks]

questions.title: Q16 — Planar Checkerboard Homography & Zhang's Constraints
questions.prompt:
A camera with intrinsic matrix K = [[1000, 0, 500], [0, 1000, 400], [0, 0, 1]] observes a planar calibration checkerboard lying on the plane Zw = 0. The camera pose relative to the board is given by rotation R = [[1, 0, 0], [0, 0.8, -0.6], [0, 0.6, 0.8]] and translation t = [0, 50, 1000]^T mm.
(a) Write out the 3 x 3 homography matrix H = K[r1 | r2 | t] relating points on the board Xw = [X, Y, 1]^T to image pixels x = [u, v, 1]^T. [4 marks]
(b) Project the checkerboard corner (100, 100) mm to image coordinates (u, v). [3 marks]
(c) Zhang's camera calibration uses the two fundamental constraints on column vectors h1, h2 of H: h1^T K^(-T) K^(-1) h2 = 0 and h1^T K^(-T) K^(-1) h1 = h2^T K^(-T) K^(-1) h2. Explain the physical geometric origin of both constraints. [3 marks]

questions.title: Q17 — Fundamental Matrix, Epipolar Lines & Point Incidence
questions.prompt:
A stereo vision rig has estimated the following Fundamental matrix: F = [[0, 0, 0], [0, 0, -0.04], [0, 0.04, 0]].
(a) Verify that det(F) = 0 and state the rank of F. [2 marks]
(b) Show that the epipole e' in the second image, satisfying F^T e' = 0, lies at infinity, and state what this implies about the camera geometry. [3 marks]
(c) For a feature point detected at x = [250, 200, 1]^T in Image 1, determine the algebraic equation of its corresponding epipolar line l' = F x = [a, b, c]^T in Image 2. [3 marks]
(d) Test whether candidate point x'A = [180, 200, 1]^T or x'B = [180, 210, 1]^T lies on this epipolar line. [2 marks]

questions.title: Q18 — Essential Matrix & Triangulation Chirality
questions.prompt:
Two calibrated cameras have identical intrinsic matrices K = I(3 x 3). The cameras have relative orientation R = I and baseline translation t = [0.2, 0, 0]^T metres (pure horizontal baseline), where t is the position of the Camera 2 centre in the Camera 1 frame, so that P2 = R^T(P1 - t).
(a) Construct the skew-symmetric matrix [t]_x and compute the Essential matrix E = [t]_x R. [3 marks]
(b) A 3D feature P is observed at normalised coordinates x1 = [0.10, 0.05, 1]^T in Camera 1 and x2 = [0.06, 0.05, 1]^T in Camera 2. Verify that x2^T E x1 = 0. [3 marks]
(c) Using the triangulation relation between horizontal disparity and depth, compute the 3D position P = (X, Y, Z)^T in metres relative to Camera 1. Verify that the point satisfies the chirality constraint (Z > 0 for both cameras). [4 marks]

questions.title: Q19 — Stereo Depth Precision & Baseline Budgeting
questions.prompt:
An autonomous vehicle uses a forward-facing stereo camera for pedestrian obstacle detection with focal length f = 1500 pixels, baseline B = 0.40 m, and image sensor resolution 1920 x 1080.
(a) A pedestrian walking in the vehicle path produces a measured disparity of d = 30.0 pixels. Calculate the exact distance Z to the pedestrian. [2 marks]
(b) If the stereo block matching algorithm has a disparity estimation error of Delta d = +/-0.5 pixels, calculate the depth uncertainty Delta Z at Z = 10.0 m and at Z = 40.0 m using the error propagation derivative |Delta Z| approximately (Z^2 / (f B)) |Delta d|. [4 marks]
(c) The vehicle braking system requires that depth uncertainty must not exceed Delta Z <= 1.5 m at a range of Z = 30.0 m. Determine the minimum baseline Bmin needed if focal length f = 1500 px and Delta d = 0.5 px remain fixed. [4 marks]

questions.title: Q20 — DLT Camera Matrix Decomposition & Optical Centre
questions.prompt:
A DLT calibration procedure yields the following 3 x 4 projection matrix: P = [[800, 0, 320, -1600], [0, 800, 240, -1200], [0, 0, 1, -5]].
(a) Determine the 3D world coordinates of the camera optical centre Cw = [X0, Y0, Z0]^T by finding the null space vector Cw_tilde = [X0, Y0, Z0, 1]^T satisfying P Cw_tilde = 0. [4 marks]
(b) Decompose the left 3 x 3 submatrix M = P(1:3, 1:3) into intrinsic matrix K and rotation matrix R such that M = K R. State the focal lengths (fx, fy), principal point (cx, cy), and Euler rotation. [3 marks]
(c) Using p4 = K t, solve for the translation vector t and verify that the optical centre satisfies Cw = -R^T t. [3 marks]
